title: How to watch the Vuelta a España 2026
content:
Cyclist
How to watch the Vuelta a España 2026

After the Giro d’Italia in May and the Tour de France last month, there’s one Grand Tour left for the men to tick off the list this year. The 81st Vuelta a España starts on Saturday 22nd August with an individual time-trial in Monaco and while Tadej Pogačar is the strong (read: only) favourite for overall victory and what would be his first red jersey, a whole host of strong riders will at least give us a fight for the podium.

After kicking off in Monaco, the race heads towards southern France in Gruissan and Andorra before entering Spanish soil on Stage 5. The race is then contained within the country’s southern regions, culminating in a hilly finale in Granada on Sunday 13th September.

Headlining the start list is recent Tour de France victor Pogačar, who is aiming to become the ninth man in history to win all three Grand Tours, joining long-time rival Jonas Vingegaard, who achieved the feat himself with victory at this year’s Giro d’Italia. Also present in Monaco will be Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost), Mattias Skjelmose (Lidl-Trek), Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM), Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Enric Mas (Movistar).

How to watch and live stream the Vuelta a España 2026

The 2026 Vuelta a España will be broadcast online through HBO Max and on TV via TNT Sports in the UK and Ireland. Throughout most of Europe, the racing will be broadcast on Eurosport with coverage also provided on RTVE/VRT in Belgium, TV2 in Denmark and RTVE in Spain.

In the United States, NBC will be airing coverage from each stage via Peacock. Next door in Canada, the racing will be available on FloBikes. For Australians, the Vuelta will be shown live on SBS whilst in New Zealand it’s on SkySport.

If it’s not being shown in your country, you may be able to watch coverage using a VPN – Virtual Private Network – which allows users to mask their IP address and watch geo-blocked content, provided they don’t need to pay for a subscription. This is also helpful for watching paid-for coverage while abroad in countries without access.
